thread:
Alex: Heads up — staging run hit a regression after the adaptive-kernel-picker change. Multi-GPU 2-node TP+PP job shows repeated all-reduce queuing, throughput drop ~35%. cc @Mina @Rick
Mina: Yep. Repro steps: run `scripts/bench_tppp.sh --model=mosaicml/7b --seq=1024 --batch=8` on the 2-node cluster. After ~180ms tokens we see sustained allreduce latency increases.
Rick: Do you have the minimal perf trace? nvprof / CUPTI samples?
Alex: Pasted the relevant bits below (trimmed):
```
[2024-09-06T15:12:45Z] kernel_select: chose fused_flash_attn_v2 for layer 4
[2024-09-06T15:12:46Z] cudaStreamCapture: beginning capture on stream 0x7f9a
[2024-09-06T15:12:46Z] cudaGraphReplay: detected host synchronization in replay path -> forcing device sync
[2024-09-06T15:12:46Z] allreduce: queued (rank0->rank1) size=64MB latency=12.4ms
[2024-09-06T15:12:46Z] allreduce: started after host-sync delay, observed 3x queue time
```
Mina: Interesting — capture started on the compute stream after we switched to the fused kernel. That kernel uses an internal host pointer check in our wrapper; might be triggering a host-call path during capture which forces replay to do a host sync.
Yvonne: I remember we added a small `cudaGetDevice()` guard in the new kernel shim to work around a driver bug. Could that be the culprit?
Alex: Likely. The shim does a `if (!device_cached) { device = cudaGetDevice(); }` inline. It was intended to be lazy but during capture it becomes a host-call and triggers `cudaStreamCapture` fallbacks.
Rick: If capture path does a host call, CUDA silently inserts host syncs on replay. That kills comm/compute overlap.
InfraBot: Deploy 17250-adaptive-kernel-picker landed in staging at 2024-09-06T15:01:12Z by CI (job #482). Rolling back is available.
Mina: Quick repro: replace fused kernel with non-fused kernel -> capture path avoids host call -> overlap restored. Numbers:
- fused: tokens/sec 720, allreduce avg wait 9.6ms
- non-fused: tokens/sec 1100, allreduce avg wait 3.1ms
Alex: Also saw KV cache prefetches being serialized behind host-syncs which increased tail latency for small prompt warmups.
Rick: Can we make the kernel shim safe for capture? Two options: 1) hoist cudaGetDevice() out of the kernel entry path during capture detection, 2) pre-warm device cache at model init so shim doesn't call it on hot path.
Yvonne: Option 2 is low-risk. We already do device enumeration in runtime init, but the shim added lazy-path to avoid overhead for headless runners. We can disable lazy-path behind `RT_SAFE_FOR_CAPTURE` compile flag.
Alex: For immediate fix I propose reverting adaptive-kernel-picker in staging and putting a guard to avoid host-calls during capture. Action items: rollback staged change, land hotfix to shim, add a unit test that runs a small graph-capture + allreduce stress.
Rick: I'll prepare a small reproducer that toggles capture mode and forces fused vs unfused kernels. Will post script and perf harness.
Mina: Also add a perf regression alert for >20% token/sec drop tied to `kernel_select` commits. That'll catch future silent regressions.
Alex: ETA for rollback + shim fix? Rick + Yvonne?
Yvonne: Can do rollback + flag in ~2 hours.
Rick: Repro script will be ready in ~1.5 hours.
Mina: I'll schedule a follow-up postmortem if rollback doesn't fully resolve; include nvprof traces and timeline.
Alex: Thanks team. Keeping this thread updated. If you hit driver oddities, ping @eng-ml-driver. :thumbsup:
